label: incidental_mention_not_reference
description: Chunk A's mention of the bridge title is an incidental n-gram or common-noun-phrase match or a homonym collision with a distinct real-world entity of the same name -- not a genuine reference to the entity described in chunk B.

label: chunk_b_no_connectable_fact
description: Chunk A's reference to the bridge is genuine
column6: but chunk B -- drawn uniformly from the bridge page per spec section 2A.1 -- covers a different part of the page (or is disambiguation-style
column7: or too generic) and holds no fact connectable to how chunk A frames the entity.

label: bridge_named_too_directly
description: Chunk A names the bridge entity so directly or centrally that a faithful question cannot avoid naming it

label: sum_of_categories
description: Sum of A+B+C, an EXACT per-note tally over all 195 decline notes (not the rounded ~51%/~42%/~6% reported in an earlier pass of this file, which back-computed to 100/82/12 -- one short of 195 -- and re-divided those integers to print false four-decimal precision on a rounded input). PROVENANCE: this is still an LLM classification of free-text notes against the three category definitions above, not a deterministic rule, and is not independently re-derivable by re-running anything: the underlying notes live in data/ws4c_cache/build_checkpoint.jsonl, which is gitignored and not committed (only questions, gold answers and chunk row IDs are committed, per CLAUDE.md). A different classifier reading the same 195 notes could draw some boundaries differently, particularly between A and B on notes that mention both a weak chunk-A reference and an unhelpful chunk B.
